notes: CD-62°1346: The authors retain it as a hypervelocity/unbound candidate even though their adopted 0.8 M⊙, 1.6 kpc case is bound; they state that the result depends on the adopted mass/distance and Galactic potential, and that it becomes unbound within the uncertainties or under other potentials (T:p1-b10, T:p7-b10, T:p8-b8, T:p8-b1). HD 5223: Newly identified in this paper as a hypervelocity CH star and explicitly unbound for any Galactic potential considered (T:p8-b8, T:p10-b9).

CD-62°1346: No equatorial coordinates (ra, dec) are reported in the supplied text/table. No numerical bound or unbound probabilities are given; at T:p7-b10 and T:p10-b6 the paper only states that whether the star is bound depends on adopted mass and Galactic potential. The ~100 kpc galactocentric value at T:p10-b1 is an orbital apogalactic distance rather than a present-day galactocentric radius, so it was not entered as galactocentric_radius. The V_GRF=577 km/s at T:p2-b1 conflicts with V_GRF=570 km/s at T:p1-b9 and V_GRF=569.8 km/s at T:p7-b10; 577 is retained with this conflict noted. The Hipparcos parallax at T:p6-b11 was explicitly disregarded by the authors but is retained as a reported value. Table 8 distances and V_GRF values are model results for the listed adopted stellar masses.

HD 5223: The target identifier is HD 5223, which the paper treats as a comparison CH star rather than the main program star; only quantities explicitly given for HD 5223 are reported. No right ascension, declination, parallax, or proper motions are reported for HD 5223 (Table 7 proper motions and the Hipparcos parallax refer to CD-62°1346), so those quantities are omitted. The paper states qualitatively that HD 5223 is unbound from the Galaxy at every Galactic potential considered (T:p1-b10, T:p10-b9), but reports no bound/unbound probability values. It quotes an escape velocity of 658 km/s (Ortega et al. 2002 potential) lower than V_GRF = 713 km/s (T:p8-b8); escape velocity is not one of the requested quantities. Regarding the Galactic center distance: T:p10-b1 states the HD 5223 orbit reaches X = 600 kpc in the XY plane and spans Z from -30 to 110 kpc from the Galactic plane (also Fig. 11 caption, T:p11-b0), but no single three-dimensional galactocentric radius is given, so galactocentric_radius is omitted.
